It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of an age where “media empires” and “electronic culture” seek to “remodel the way we think about truth,” and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the distinction between the breath of the Almighty and the cold calculations of machines in this digital hour? [13, 196, 1242, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by a “spirit of fraud” that suggests human uniqueness can be replaced by a clever algorithm, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “history is His story”—a single, cohesive account of God’s glory that no machine can truly narrate? [1, 13, 20, 310, 1260, 1407, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to offer “spiritual placebos” or suggest that the Bible needs the help of “modern psychology,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs our souls by His complete and perfect Law [1, 4, 11, 28, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the rise of technologies that mimic human knowledge is not an “administrative anomaly” but a context in which we must “examine everything carefully” to distinguish the “glittery lookalike from the genuine commodity” [220, 354, 1143, 1532, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Pattern of Divine Creation vs. Creaturely Imitation**

**Verse**
“So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them” (Genesis 1:27). [758, 1145, 1166, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scriptures teach that humanity is the “crowning point of creation,” and being made in God’s image defines man’s “unique relation to God,” setting him “apart from the animals” and all mechanical constructs [1160, 1166, 1313, 1322, Conversation History]. God created man in His image as a living being capable of embodying His communicable attributes (Genesis 1:26, “Then God said, ‘Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness’ ”) [758, 759, 1144, 1166, Conversation History]. The “record of history” shows that the first “imitation” occurred in the Garden when the serpent questioned God’s Word to sow doubt (Genesis 3:1, “Now the serpent was more cunning than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said to the woman, ‘Has God indeed said, “You shall not eat of every tree of the garden”?’ ”) [762, 1148, 1176, 1339, 1503, Conversation History]. Satan’s goal is to offer a “designer religion” that promises we can “be like God” through our own efforts (Genesis 3:5, “ ‘For God knows that in the day you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil’ ”) [763, 1180, 1339, 1381, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by technologies that claim to “know” or “create,” for “your life is not your own” because “you were bought at a price” by the King (1 Corinthians 6:20, “For you were bought at a price; therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s”) [249, 272, 795, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that a machine lacks the “breath of life” given only to man (Genesis 2:7, “And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being”) [1171, 1197, 1328, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Tower of Babel to Digital Empires**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, the builders of Babel sought to “make a name for ourselves” through human ingenuity (Genesis 11:4, “And they said, ‘Come, let us build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top is in the heavens; let us make a name for ourselves’ ”) [846, 901, 1159, 1193, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” showing that our “citizenship is in heaven” and we find “repose of the soul” not in our “building enterprises” but in the “finished work” of Christ (Philippians 3:20, “For our citizenship is in heaven, from which we also eagerly wait for the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ”) [13, 21, 26, 28, 142, 1028, 1199, 1203, 1313, 1320, 1426, 1445, 1529, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Test of Accuracy and the Spirit of Truth**

**Verse**
“ ‘When a prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the thing does not happen or come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord has not spoken; the prophet has spoken it presumptuously; you shall not be afraid of him’ ” (Deuteronomy 18:22). [47, 427, 472, 1101, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that “true knowledge” is “that which is consistent with the mind, will, character, glory, and being of God” [1280, 1306, 1493, Conversation History]. God’s truth is “propositional” and “absolute,” and any “self-proclaimed prophet” or technology that delivers “erroneous and corrupt” information proves itself to be a “spirit of fraud” [42, 448, 1100, 1301, 1325, 1333, 1503, Conversation History]. Scripture handles the “clamor and tumult” of those seeking “fresh revelation” by demanding 100 percent accuracy, for “no lie is of the truth” (1 John 2:21, “I have not written to you because you do not know the truth, but because you know it, and that no lie is of the truth”) [13, 46, 113, 382, 1300, 1314, 1503, 1512, Conversation History]. When technology “generates” knowledge that is “unverified,” it risks becoming a “word freshly spoken from heaven” that is actually a “counterfeit” (1 John 4:1, “Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God; because many false prophets have gone out into the world”) [319, 329, 354, 431, 1423, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You must “discipline your mind” to “examine everything carefully,” refusing to accept “subjective impressions” as divine guidance (1 Thessalonians 5:21, “Test all things; hold fast what is good”) [82, 90, 116, 294, 325, 1017, 1313, 1408, 1515, 1709, Conversation History]. “Trade in your worry for trust” in the “only source of absolute divine authority,” for “the Word of our God stands forever” (Isaiah 40:8, “The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever”) [11, 21, 24, 68, 94, 201, 1104, 1117, 1118, 1132, 1143, 1198, 1306, 1312, 1408, 1420, 1515, 1684, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Jurisdiction**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “false prophecy” was a “capital offense” because it “counseled rebellion against the LORD” (Deuteronomy 13:5, “ ‘But that prophet or that dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, because he has spoken in order to turn you away from the LORD your God’ ”) [41, 517, 582, 779, 1316, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “warfare,” teaching that while we “do not war according to the flesh,” we must “contend earnestly for the faith” using the “sword of the Spirit” (2 Corinthians 10:4, “For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal but mighty in God for pulling down strongholds”) [13, 21, 32, 43, 92, 113, 201, 874, 1081, 1313, 1325, 1408, 1440, 1474, 1479, 1480, 1515, 1520, 1601, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Engaging Technology with a Renewed Mind**

**Verse**
“And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God” (Romans 12:2). [81, 746, 799, 876, 1550, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer**—warns that a mind that is constantly fed by “media empires” will be “tossed to and fro... by the trickery of men” (Ephesians 4:14, “that we should no longer be children, tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men”) [203, 296, 327, 437, 1435, 1506, 1521, Conversation History]. We are called to “discipline our minds for action” and not let technology “shave off the edges” of the truth for the sake of “consumer-driven culture” (1 Peter 1:13, “Therefore gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and rest your hope fully upon the grace that is to be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ”) [21, 28, 82, 101, 116, 279, 310, 1434, 1436, 1503, Conversation History]. “Spiritual formation” involves the “Holy Spirit and the Spirit-inspired Scriptures” which are “wholly sufficient” to equip the saint, rendering “man-made representations” unnecessary (2 Timothy 3:16–17, “All Scripture is given by inspiration of God... that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work”) [562, 595, 727, 859, 922, 1062, 1097, 1118, 1312, 1331, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “opinion polls” or “pagan mystery religions,” but instead “boast in this, that you know and understand Me” (Jeremiah 9:24, “ ‘But let him who glories glory in this, that he understands and knows Me, that I am the LORD’ ”) [51, 123, 145, 163, 209, 526, 657, 720, 721, 1398, 1406, 1448, 1503, Conversation History]. Your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” by using all “faculties... for His glory,” ensuring that technology remains a tool and not a master [11, 12, 101, 120, 121, 172, 361, 1406, 1450, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “national greatness” was a “temporal sign” of God’s blessing, yet God “removed kings” who “rejected the word of the LORD” for their own devices (1 Samuel 15:23, “ ‘For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He also has rejected you from being king’ ”) [15, 17, 342, 409, 1078, 1173, 1183, 1313, 1353, 1519, 1533, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “vision of Christ,” revealing that we are being “transformed into the same image” by the Spirit, not by the “cunning craftiness” of human-built systems (2 Corinthians 3:18, “But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory”) [218, 382, 551, 569, 612, 618, 749, 814, 868, 870, 1018, 1218, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Weighing of Truth and Imitation**

**Verse**
“ ‘But outside are dogs and sorcerers and sexually immoral and murderers and idolaters, and whoever loves and practices a lie’ ” (Revelation 22:15). [1002, 1081, 1102, 1512, 1605, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of “unrighteous deception” by pointing to the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 16, 20, 21, 23, 24, 31, 103, 136, 182, 815, 1081, 1199, 1311, 1315, 1402, 1403, 1500, 1515, 1524, 1532, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. Every ruler and “building enterprise” that seeks to “write themselves into God’s office” using technology will ultimately be “weighed on the scales and found deficient” (Daniel 5:27, “ ‘You have been weighed on the scales and found deficient’ ”) [11, 15, 30, 37, 324, 412, 1061, 1143, 1230, 1402, 1450, 1502, 1720, Conversation History]. On the Day of the Lord, every human “monument of pride” and “storage city” will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away,” but the “Lord Savior” will “judge between the nations” and His “everlasting dominion” will remain (Psalm 102:3, “For my days are consumed like smoke, and my bones are burned like a hearth”) [11, 32, 35, 37, 43, 63, 789, 818, 836, 852, 940, 976, 1143, 1211, 1233, 1315, 1402, 1408, 1460, 1515, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “perfect justice will come” from the “Lord, the righteous Judge” (1 Thessalonians 1:10, “and to wait for His Son from heaven, whom He raised from the dead, even Jesus who delivers us from the wrath to come”) [13, 14, 21, 24, 92, 94, 109, 121, 201, 313, 352, 412, 470, 719, 740, 745, 816, 822, 830, 852, 869, 883, 903, 940, 943, 948, 1009, 1033, 1039, 1121, 1132, 1143, 1162, 1197, 1203, 1251, 1255, 1257, 1259, 1282, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1503, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” the “spirit of truth” is more than sufficient for your every need (Psalm 138:2, “I will worship toward Your holy temple, And praise Your name For Your lovingkindness and Your truth; For You have magnified Your word above all Your name”) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 313, 352, 412, 576, 602, 630, 788, 852, 869, 921, 957, 1012, 1035, 1132, 1143, 1183, 1214, 1300, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1315, 1407, 1408, 1420, 1441, 1450, 1515, 1572, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 262, 285, 300, 311, 324, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 834, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: to an acceptance of life ‘as it is,’ to accept it on its own terms—which means acknowledging the inevitability of the way it works—is to surrender a Christian view of God.”4 A part of the right understanding of and attitude toward God’s will is what might be called a sense of righteous rebellion. To be dedicated to God’s will necessitates being opposed to Satan’s. To pray “Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven” is to rebel against the notion that sin is normal and inevitable and therefore should be tolerated. When you are wholly committed to seeing God’s will done on earth, you will rebel against the world system of ungodliness. You will renounce all things that dishonor and reject Christ. And you will also confront the disobedience of believers. Impotence in prayer leads us, however unwillingly, to strike a truce with evil. When you accept what is, you abandon a Christian view of God and His plan for redemptive history.

here refers to one’s pattern of life or conduct. God’s Word cultivates the godly attitudes, thoughts, and actions that will keep trials and temptations from overwhelming us. To understand the relationship between the three, consider this analogy: If a police officer sees someone who is about to violate the law, the officer will restrain that person. Similarly, godly attitudes and thoughts produced by the Word act as police officers to restrain the flesh before it commits a crime against the standard of God’s Word. But if they aren’t on duty, they can’t restrain the flesh, and the flesh is free to violate the law of God.
